_readme: Human-reviewed disagreements between the RagnaPlace API (laro-pt) and the
divine-pride LATAM stat block, for fields the two sources both publish.
tools/scrape-mobs.mjs cross-checks every overlapping field and refuses to write
mobs.json if it finds a disagreement that is not listed here. A disagreement
means either the crawler broke or the two databases genuinely differ, and only
a human can tell those apart — so acknowledging one is a deliberate edit to
this file, not a flag on the command line.
An entry matches only while BOTH recorded values still hold. If either source
changes its number the entry stops matching and the build fails again, which
is the point: an acknowledgement covers one specific known difference, never
the field in general.
`prefer` picks which source's value mobs.json publishes for that one field:
"ragnaplace" (the default, and what every pre-existing row already carries) or
"divine-pride". res/mres are normally unaffected — divine-pride is their only
source.
`"resistances": "unknown"` is the exception, and it is deliberately hard to
reach: it says the divine-pride record for this monster describes something
other than the monster we mean, so its res/mres are not a measurement of
anything. That monster then publishes res/mres NULL rather than divine-pride's
number. Use it only when the record is demonstrably about a different thing —
a dummy row, another episode's monster — never merely because a value looks
surprising. Publishing 0 from a bogus record is the exact failure this whole
second source exists to prevent.

accepted.why: Event clone. Its base 1087 ORK_HERO is element level 2 on both sources, so divine-pride's 4 here matches neither base nor the sibling clone 2094 (which says 2) — this one is NOT confirmed by a base monster. Adopted with the rest of the family by explicit decision, on the strength of the pattern rather than a direct check. RagnaPlace stores propertyLevel 1 for every one of the 20 E_*/EVENT_* event clones, whose base monsters span element levels 1-4 — a uniform default, not data. On the 13 clones whose base could be identified, divine-pride's value equals the base's exactly, and both sources already agree on the base.
